evidence.description: Tracker columns consumed or used to derive its inspection intensity variables.
evidence.quote:
import excel "PCAOB Report Tracker.xlsx", sheet("Formatted for Merge") firstrow clear
format insp_repdte %d
format insp_startdte %d
format insp_enddte %d 
replace no_engage_ins = " " if no_engage_ins == "NA"
replace FIclientsinspected = " " if FIclientsinspected == "NA"
destring FIclientsinspected, replace
destring no_engage_ins, replace
replace inspected = 0 if inspected == . 

//Create Inspection Intensity Variables for primary analysis and various scalars
bysort auditor_key_msu: egen estFIclientsinspected = mean(FIclientsinspected)
bysort auditor_key_msu: egen est_no_engage_ins = mean(no_engage_ins)
gen subst_find_intensity = tot_substant_find/tot_issuers_finding
replace subst_find_intensity = 0 if tot_issuers_finding == 0
gen both_find_intensity = tot_both_find/tot_issuers_finding
replace both_find_intensity = 0 if tot_issuers_finding == 0

//Scaled by Total FI clients inspected 
gen subst_find_intensity_FI = tot_substant_find/FIclientsinspected

//Scaled by Total Estimated FI clients inspected 
gen subst_find_intensity_estFI = tot_substant_find/estFIclientsinspected

//Scaled by Total engagements inspected 
gen subst_find_intensity_insp = tot_substant_find/no_engage_ins

//Scaled by Estimated Total engagements inspected 
gen subst_find_intensity_estinsp = tot_substant_find/est_no_engage_ins

//Gen non-ALL Finding Indicators & intensity
gen count_non_all_issuers = tot_issuers_finding - tot_issuers_all
gen non_all_find = 0
replace non_all_find = 1 if count_non_all_issuers > 0
gen non_all_intensity = count_non_all_issuers/tot_issuers_finding
replace non_all_intensity = 0 if tot_issuers_finding == 0
gen non_all_intensity_insp = count_non_all_issuers/no_engage_ins
gen non_all_intensity_estinsp = count_non_all_issuers/est_no_engage_ins
gen non_all_intensity_FIinsp = count_non_all_issuers/FIclientsinspected
gen non_all_intensity_FIestinsp = count_non_all_issuers/estFIclientsinspected

evidence.description: Datasheet describes the FDIC Call Report and WRDS FR Y-9C source history and manual auditor identification.
evidence.quote:
Bank level data (Call reports) were obtained from the FDIC’s Summary of Depository Institution
data (https://www5.fdic.gov/sdi/download_large_list_outside.asp) on September 27, 2017 for the
years 2005-2016 and on June 25, 2019, for years 2017-2018.
Holding company level data (FR Y-9C) were obtained from the Wharton Research Data
Services’ (WRDS) Bank Regulatory Bank Holding Company database on July 24, 2017 for the
years 2005-2016 and on May 22, 2018 for year 2017. The names of the bank auditors were
manually cleaned and assigned unique identifiers to allow for analysis. Public bank-years were
identified from the holding company data based on field rssd9056. The year-end FR Y-9C was
merged to appropriate bank call reports as of year-end in order to obtain the bank auditor
identification.
PCAOB inspection reports for the sample auditors were obtained from the Firm Inspection
Reports page on the PCAOB’s website
(https://pcaobus.org/Inspections/Reports/Pages/default.aspx) on various dates in 2017, 2018 and
2019. These reports were manually reviewed by Sarah Stuber to identify the total number of
findings and the total number of findings related to the allowance for loan losses, as well as the
dates of inspection fieldwork and final inspection report date. Chris Hogan manually reviewed a
sample of the coded reports for accuracy of classifications. The manually collected information
from the PCAOB inspection reports was then merged into the bank and auditor dataset to create
a final dataset for analysis.

evidence.description: Appendix A describes manual coding of PCAOB report findings and review years/classification.
evidence.quote:
The data for the calculation of FINDING_INTENSITY and FINDING_INTENSITY_BOTH

are obtained from a manual review of PCAOB inspection reports from 2006-2017. An individual

issuer is deemed to have a substantive ALL-related finding if an inspection finding specifically

references the ALL and is related to direct testing of the ALL, including the evaluation of either

qualitative or quantitative inputs into the ALL calculation. These inputs include items such as

evaluation of the loss factors, recalculation of charge-off history, consideration of the charge-off

windows and consideration of inputs into asset valuations for determining specific allowances

necessary for non-performing assets. An example of a finding considered to be an ALL-related

substantive finding is included in Panel B below. An issuer is deemed to have an ALL-related

control finding, if there is a specific mention of failure to properly evaluate the design of controls

or failure to properly test the controls related to the ALL. Examples of issuers with both control

and substantive ALL-related findings is included in Panel C below. Issuers where there were

findings noted, but the findings did not mention the ALL calculation or key inputs to the ALL

calculation are considered to have non-ALL findings. Due to the clear distinction of control and

non-control related findings in the language used by the PCAOB, as well as specific reference to

the ALL estimate, classification of the findings involves minimal subjectivity, as seen in the

examples below. Each report was initially reviewed and coded by one coauthor for consistency in

classification of findings. A second coauthor reviewed a sample of the coded reports for accuracy

of classifications.

actions.description: Locate or document compatible versions of the five exact inputs and verify their complete contracts before running the supplied workflow. Keep prepared author files as the primary input route; any raw-source reconstruction is conditional and must not replace the authored definitions.
steps: Stage PCAOB Report Tracker.xlsx with the exact Formatted for Merge sheet and verify first-row/imported names for all required fields, including annu_insp (dropped before recreation) and repyr (needed by the later merge, not created in Section A).

Stage 2005-2018 Bank and Holding Company Data for Analysis.dta and check every expected field; preserve distinct lnatresr/lnatres and lnrenrot/lnrenres references until their actual source meanings are confirmed.

Verify the Auditor Sample.dta auditor_key_msu lookup is unique and matches the described selected auditor set. Verify State Number Assignment.dta stalp and Fed Reserve Numbers.dta fed lookup uniqueness, coverage, and actual non-key payload columns.

Confirm the bank panel period, ordering, missing-year gaps and within-bank rows needed by the code’s _n-1/_n-2/_n+1/_n+2/_n+3 constructions. These are row offsets, not gap-aware calendar-year lags/leads.

Preserve the whole loaded bank input for the authored winsor operations, which occur before keep if repyr > 2005; do not recalculate cutoffs on only the final sample or create a 1991 raw-data dependency from the hard-coded chargeoff constants.

In a working copy, set a relative runtime working directory containing the five input files, extract/reflow the supplied TXT as a Stata do-file if desired, then run Sections A → B → C in order: A creates PCAOB Inspection Findings.dta; C consumes it, then merges State Number Assignment and Fed Reserve Numbers before saving File for Analysis.dta.

If PCAOB Report Tracker.xlsx cannot be obtained, use the official PCAOB report page as a candidate public source and follow Appendix A’s manual report classification procedure; confirm 2006–2017 report coverage, report-date-to-repyr mapping, and the auditor_key_msu crosswalk before producing the exact tracker. The detailed Part I.A/Part I.B series described on the current page starts with 2018 annual / 2019 triennial reports and is not a substitute for the earlier manual review.

If the prepared bank panel cannot be obtained, assess the public FDIC plus FFIEC NIC route first: obtain the Call Report/SDI and FR Y-9C source files, then confirm source columns, RSSD/auditor identifiers, year-end joins, bank-panel aliases and row history against the exact prepared-file contract. The public route can replace WRDS if it supplies compatible fields/IDs; use the datasheet’s WRDS route only as an alternative if needed and available.
